title: Develop
description: A wooden utility pole shot from its foot, straight up through its crossarms and cables into summer cumulus, coming up like a print in a darkroom tray, except that the developer runs through the scene's depth rather than across the paper. It opens as a print does, the darkest, nearest wood first, at the foot of the pole, and climbs it. Drag and a thin band of warm light carries on through the depth; start from a blank sheet on the sky and it runs the other way, from the far sky towards you. Behind it the photograph has arrived, sharp and in full colour. Ahead of it the scene is not there yet: the sky a faint, light latent print in its own blue, out of focus by as much as the depth still to cover, the cloud melting rather than breaking into bokeh, and the pole and its cables not there at all, a latent image being invisible, so they come up out of the sky at the front, always sharp, the frame's one crisp anchor: the structure develops along its own length, up the pole and out of the knot along each cable and brace, every wire one unbroken stroke. In the sky the depth is the cloud's own, so the cores come up first and the front threads the cumulus. Let go and the front carries your speed, then the print settles. Drag back to undo it.
intent: One depth-keyed reveal from herb's CrowdVolt depth research (factory/reality/crowdvolt-depth-heroes.md: a front sweeps a key 0..1 through depth; scan, focus pull, assemble, strata), finished as a title sequence with the quality of a print coming up in a darkroom tray, in the summer-film genre (factory/reality/genre-spec.md). References: Saul Bass's and Pablo Ferro's title sequences that reveal an image by a moving edge (https://www.artofthetitle.com/), and the darkroom print emerging in developer (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photographic_developer).

sources.author: Dina Lydia (@dinazina)
sources.note: 3593x2736, Seattle, a worm's-eye frame from the foot of the pole: its sides converge on a vanishing point in the upper third of the frame, the cables and braces radiate out of it, cumulus all round. Cropped to a full-width 3:2 band (rows 200-2595) and shipped at 2400x1600. Re-plated from the earlier PJH (@dokae) catenary mast in Ine (unsplash 6DHLBwmRkOw), a 40-degree look up that read as an ordinary snapshot. Depth Anything V2 Small (tools/depth/depth_hr.py), prepared as in herb's notes (percentile normalise, median, dilate near values, slight blur). Split into two layers: the sky with the pole, crossarms, braces and every cable painted out (LaMa, big-lama ONNX, at half size through a mask dilated well past the silhouettes, matched to the sky round each hole in log light, grain put back; shown only a few pixels past the structure, the photo's own sky beyond), and the structure as a known-background matte over it (alpha = (I-B).(F-B)/|F-B|^2; cables found by a black-hat on luma; the bright hardware, lit braces and insulators, found as narrow features lighter or darker than the local sky that hang off the structure, and matted against the painted sky; the matte is pulled against a log-light normalised-convolution fill). The structure develops not by its depth (the depth model sees a two-pixel cable only in patches, so the wires came up as tapered slivers and floating fragments) but by its reach: the geodesic distance from the pole's foot measured inside the matte, monotonic outward along every cable and brace and the same across a cable's width (bake.py --reach, reach.png, 16 bit). The sky key's distance term is measured from the zenith the pole points at, and the sky is graded round it in the bake, in log light: deep cobalt overhead opening to a paler cyan at the corners, the cloud's rims turned off lilac to a cyan-grey and its tops warmed to a neutral. Bake: tools/depth/bakes/develop/bake.py. The structure is all that is kept of this photograph: its own sky (a pale cerulean with small, flat-white curds) was replaced (bake.py --sky) by two horizon photographs of congestus, CC0 (next sources), wound round the zenith by a stereographic look-up so the towers ring the frame's edges and lean in on the pole's vanishing point, the thin cloud above them cleared to open cobalt overhead; put in behind the same matte, the structure taken as plate - (1 - alpha) x fill and laid over it, and graded for the frame: cobalt round the zenith opening to cyan, sunlit warm-neutral tops on a shoulder under paper white, the curds' local contrast pulled back, the shadowed undersides a lifted skylight blue (hue ~208); the sky key measured again from the warped cloud.

sources.author: John Robert McPherson (Wikimedia Commons)
sources.note: 4608x3456 (fetched at 3840x2880), a row of congestus over the same shore, horizon at row 2570. The half of the sky to the right of the pole. Both re-plated by a radial look-up round the zenith (bake.py _sky_lookup): azimuth kept, radius stereographic (v = ln tan(theta/2)), each photo's horizon along the frame's edge and one photo per half turn, so the towers stand round the rim of the dome and lean in on the vanishing point the pole runs into. The halves meet under the pole and above the zenith. Replaces the eye-level CC0 cumulus plate (Raysonho, BlueSkyWhiteClouds17), whose flat curds read as a backdrop.
